code.originalText: Genetic results, classification and risk, fitness for treatment, early palliative care, and day 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax

text.paragraph: Genetic results, classification and risk, fitness for treatment, and the start of induction. [S]

Mrs. Joliot-Curie returns twelve days after the marrow biopsy to review the genetic results and decide on treatment. She has had blood counts twice a week; she felt better after the red cell transfusion but is tired again and now rests for part of each afternoon and has stopped going to the laboratory. No fever, bleeding beyond bruising, or infection. She had her echocardiogram, lung function tests and ECG earlier today. Her hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests were negative, and she is not immune to hepatitis B. She has read the trial reports on the treatment options and has questions. She met the palliative care team this morning. [S]

Abnormal results of pulmonary function studies

list.item:
Acute myeloid leukemia with mutated TP53 and a complex karyotype; ELN 1951 adverse risk (C92.00). Cytogenetics show a complex karyotype with loss of chromosome 5q material and of chromosome 7 (45,XX,del(5)(q14q34),-7,-17,+mar in 16 of 20 cells), and the molecular panel shows a TP53 mutation at a variant allele frequency of 41 percent, with no NPM1, FLT3, IDH1, IDH2 or CEBPA mutation. By the WHO 1951 classification this is AML, myelodysplasia-related (defined by the complex karyotype); by the ICC 1951 it is AML with mutated TP53. Neither system's post-cytotoxic-therapy (therapy-related) label applies, because that label requires earlier chemotherapy or radiotherapy given as treatment, whereas her exposure was occupational; we record the leukemia as following occupational exposure to ionizing radiation, and its genetics are those typical of radiation-associated and therapy-related myeloid neoplasms. ELN 1951 genetic risk is adverse. Fitness: ECOG 2 and a DLCO of 58 percent of predicted (HCT-CI score 3) make her ineligible for intensive induction under the VIALE-A criteria; intensive chemotherapy also gives poor results in TP53-mutated AML. After discussing the options, including intensive induction and clinical trials (none open to her here), she chooses azacitidine with venetoclax, aiming for remission and an allogeneic transplant. Dr. Engquist-Mensah's team will lead treatment. [S]
Admit today for cycle 1: azacitidine 115 mg (75 mg/m2) on days 1 to 7; venetoclax 10 mg on day 1, 20 mg on day 2, 50 mg on day 3, then 70 mg daily from day 4, the dose with posaconazole.
Tumor lysis monitoring during the ramp-up, with allopurinol and fluids.
Bone marrow on day 21 to 28.
Transplant center evaluation and unrelated donor search now.

Reduced lung gas transfer from old tuberculous scarring (R94.2). DLCO 58 percent and FEV1 76 percent of predicted. The echocardiogram is normal (ejection fraction 62 percent) and the QTc 428 ms. [S]
Counts toward her transplant comorbidity index; repeat lung function before transplant.

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation (Z57.1). Records not yet received. [S]
Chase the written request.

Emergency department at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more. Next scheduled visit 1955-10-19: day 22 of cycle 1: bone marrow response, transfusion and infection review, and stopping venetoclax for count recovery. [S]
